rule: A creature is one species id plus per-creature rows (biota), not a class per creature. Each body part carries damage type, damage value, variance fraction, base armour, armour per damage type, a hit-height weight and twelve hit-zone weights. An attack cone names a part index; special attacks use the breath part; otherwise a random part with non-zero damage is used. Palette template and shade set the look, and the corpse copies both on death. On treasure create-list rows a non-zero shade is used as a probability, handled in 0-1 chunks.
keep: Species id plus palette: one id, one look, reused across rows
Corpse and loot inherit the creature look on death
Attack cone telegraph: one named zone lit before the strike
Small variance per body part instead of a fixed number
Shade as a 0-1 probability on loot rows
change: 12 hit zones become 3 (head, body, legs) on a 375-wide phone
8 armour types become our 3 damage families
World rows live in our data store, not SQL patch files
Species names and any donor stat rows are not reused
look_test: One creature at 375 wide, twice: a plain strike and a three-zone telegraph (head, body, legs) that lights the zone about half a second before the hit. Dom judges whether he can tell the zone in under one second and whether the corpse reads as the same creature. Build only the telegraph and the palette copy; no new art.
